001: Have you started preparing the presentation for history class?
Not yet, I'm a bit lost. I don't even know where to begin.
How about choosing a topic you like? It gets much easier.
That's true. I really like the part about the Industrial Revolution.
Great! Then start by researching that and put together a simple outline.
Good idea. I'll do that tonight.
002: Can you help me organize the slides for my presentation?
Sure! Show me what you have so far.
I only wrote the title and a few random bullet points.
Alright. We can divide it into introduction, development, and conclusion.
That makes sense. Do you think I should add more images?
Definitely, but don't overdo it. Just to make it look nicer.
003: I'm nervous about presenting in front of the class tomorrow.
Relax, you studied a lot and you know the subject well.
I know, but I'm afraid I'll forget everything when the time comes.
One tip: rehearse out loud today, even if you're by yourself.
I'll try to do that after dinner.
If you want, we can rehearse together over a video call.
004: Have you finished the slides for the geography presentation?
Almost. I just need to review the data part.
Can I take a look for you? I'm good with that.
Really? That would be great. I get confused with those charts.
No problem. Send me the file and I'll review it now.
Perfect, thank you so much for the help.
005: The teacher asked us to present in pairs, are you in?
I'm in. We get along well, it'll be easy.
So we can split the parts: I'll take the introduction.
Deal. I'll take the examples and the conclusion.
We need to rehearse together beforehand, right?
Of course. How about we meet at the library tomorrow?
006: Do you know how long the presentation needs to be?
I think about ten minutes, at most.
Wow, that's longer than I imagined.
Yeah, but you can speak calmly and explain each point well.
True. That way you can even interact with the audience.
Exactly. A good presentation isn't just reading the slide.
007: I finished my script, but I think it's too long.
Let me see. Wow, there really is a lot of text.
I don't know what to cut, everything seems important.
Try summarizing each part into one main sentence.
Good. That way I can see what's essential.
Right. Then we'll put the slides together based on that summary.
008: Are you going to use any visual aids in your presentation?
Yes, I am. I thought about using some short videos.
That's cool! It makes the presentation much more dynamic.
Yeah, but I need to be careful not to go over the time.
You can time yourself while you rehearse.
Good idea. I'll do that to make sure it stays within the limit.
009: I was really nervous during my presentation today.
But you did great! Nobody noticed anything.
You think? I forgot a part in the middle.
It didn't even show. You handled the situation really well.
Thanks. At least now I know what to improve for next time.
That's right. Every presentation is a chance to learn.
010: The teacher commented on our presentation, did you see?
I did. He praised our organization quite a bit.
What a relief! I was afraid I had come across as confused.
On the contrary, he said we were very clear.
I'm glad all our effort was worth it.
For sure. Next time, we already know how to do it.
